questions.prompt: Explain finding F1 and finding F2: how two sequential writes hide behind one failure message, and why the screen's own map duplicates the helper's policy.

keyPoints.text: The sale screen awaits the sale write and may then await a batch status write.
keyPoints.quote: then may await `updatePigBatch({ ...batch, status: "sold_out", ... })`

keyPoints.text: If the second write fails the sale is already stored.
keyPoints.quote: the sale is already persisted under `piggery_sales`

keyPoints.text: Retrying an add therefore duplicates the sale.
keyPoints.quote: A user who retries an *add* creates a duplicate sale

keyPoints.text: No mechanism makes the two keys commit together.
keyPoints.quote: Nothing spans the two AsyncStorage keys

keyPoints.text: One fix is to stop persisting a status that display already derives.
keyPoints.quote: stop persisting a derived status

keyPoints.text: The screen rebuilds the collection with the old silent map pattern.
keyPoints.quote: the screen re-implements the old silent `map`

keyPoints.text: That is only harmless because the context update already threw.
keyPoints.quote: It is harmless today only because `updateSale` already threw for a missing id

questions.prompt: Explain findings F3 and F4 and the review rubric: what is lost by bare catch blocks, why a stale closure defeats the guard, and what a reviewer must reject.

keyPoints.text: Every form screen catches without binding the error.
keyPoints.quote: All six form screens use `catch {` without binding the error

keyPoints.text: As a result different failure kinds look the same to users and logs.
keyPoints.quote: Identity, validation, and storage failures are indistinguishable to the user and to any log.

keyPoints.text: Each callback writes whatever array its closure captured.
keyPoints.quote: Each callback writes the array captured by its closure.

keyPoints.text: A stale array containing a deleted id passes the guard and brings the record back.
keyPoints.quote: passes the guard and resurrects the record

keyPoints.text: That needs a version check or re-read, not a stronger helper.
keyPoints.quote: Preventing that needs a version check or a re-read before write

keyPoints.text: The rubric requires a missing identity to throw before any await.
keyPoints.quote: missing identity throws before any `await`

keyPoints.text: Patches that swallow the error and claim success are rejected.
keyPoints.quote: catches the error and reports success
